Niacinamide.does: regulates oil production, strengthens the skin barrier, calms inflammation, fades post-acne marks
Niacinamide.side_effects: rare mild flushing at high concentrations
Niacinamide.beginner_tip: start with 5%, no patch test needed like with stronger actives

Salicylic Acid.does: oil-soluble exfoliant that penetrates pores to clear oil and dead skin buildup
Salicylic Acid.beginner_tip: start low frequency, always follow with moisturizer

Hyaluronic Acid.does: humectant that draws water into the skin for hydration
Hyaluronic Acid.best_for: all skin types, including sensitive and dry
Hyaluronic Acid.side_effects: none common; apply to damp skin and seal with moisturizer
Hyaluronic Acid.beginner_tip: apply to damp skin, then seal with a moisturizer

Retinol.does: vitamin A derivative that speeds up cell turnover
Retinol.best_for: most skin types once introduced slowly
Retinol.side_effects: dryness, peeling, sun sensitivity when starting out
Retinol.when: PM only, always with SPF the next morning
Retinol.beginner_tip: start 2x per week, increase gradually over weeks

Ascorbic Acid.does: antioxidant that brightens skin and protects against environmental damage
Ascorbic Acid.best_for: normal, oily, combination skin; sensitive skin may need a gentler derivative
Ascorbic Acid.side_effects: can irritate sensitive skin at high strength
Ascorbic Acid.beginner_tip: start with a stable derivative like sodium ascorbyl phosphate

Ceramide NP.does: lipid that occurs naturally in skin and helps form the protective barrier
Ceramide NP.beginner_tip: safe to use daily from day one

Azelaic Acid.does: gentle multi-tasking acid, tolerated even by sensitive and rosacea-prone skin
Azelaic Acid.side_effects: mild tingling on application, usually temporary
Azelaic Acid.beginner_tip: start daily at 10%, prescription strengths are higher and need a dermatologist

Glycolic Acid.does: AHA that exfoliates the skin's surface to improve texture and tone
Glycolic Acid.best_for: normal, oily, combination skin; go easy if sensitive
Glycolic Acid.side_effects: irritation, sun sensitivity, redness if overused

Alpha-Arbutin.does: tyrosinase-inhibiting brightening agent that reduces melanin production
Alpha-Arbutin.best_for: most skin types, including sensitive skin

Centella Asiatica Leaf Extract.does: soothing, anti-inflammatory extract that supports barrier repair

Squalane.does: lightweight emollient that mimics skin's natural lipids to lock in moisture
Squalane.when: AM and/or PM, often as a last step

Zinc PCA.does: helps regulate oil production, mild antibacterial properties
Zinc PCA.beginner_tip: pairs well with niacinamide for oil control

Panthenol.does: humectant and soothing agent that supports hydration and barrier repair
Panthenol.best_for: all skin types, especially dry or irritated
Panthenol.beginner_tip: very safe, no patch test typically needed

Lactic Acid.does: gentler AHA that exfoliates and also has humectant properties
Lactic Acid.best_for: normal to dry skin, or sensitive skin wanting gentle exfoliation
Lactic Acid.side_effects: irritation or sun sensitivity if overused

Tranexamic Acid.does: brightening ingredient that reduces melanin production
Tranexamic Acid.beginner_tip: pairs well with niacinamide and vitamin C

Bakuchiol.does: plant-derived retinol alternative, similar cell-turnover benefits with less irritation
Bakuchiol.best_for: sensitive skin or those who can't tolerate retinol
Bakuchiol.beginner_tip: gentler starting point than retinol, still worth patch testing

Peptide.does: signal proteins that support collagen production and skin repair
Peptide.best_for: most skin types, especially aging-prone skin
Peptide.beginner_tip: safe daily, pairs well with most other actives

Tocopherol.does: antioxidant that protects skin from environmental damage and supports moisture barrier
Tocopherol.side_effects: rare; can be comedogenic in oil-based formulas for very acne-prone skin
Tocopherol.beginner_tip: usually already combined into other products like vitamin C serums

Ferulic Acid.does: antioxidant that stabilizes and boosts the effectiveness of vitamin C
Ferulic Acid.beginner_tip: usually already combined into vitamin C serums

Allantoin.does: soothing, skin-conditioning ingredient that supports healing and hydration
Allantoin.best_for: all skin types, especially sensitive or irritated skin
Allantoin.beginner_tip: often paired with stronger actives to offset irritation

Camellia Sinensis Leaf Extract.best_for: most skin types, including oily and acne-prone

Adenosine.does: soothing ingredient with mild anti-wrinkle signaling properties
Adenosine.best_for: most skin types, popular in mature/anti-aging formulas

Beta-Glucan.does: soothing, hydrating polysaccharide that supports barrier repair

conflict_classes.gentle_universal: No known conflicts with other actives. Safe to combine freely.
conflict_classes.strong_exfoliant_night: Increases cell turnover / sensitivity. Avoid stacking with other members of this class on the same night; alternate nights instead.
conflict_classes.ph_sensitive_am: Works best in a low-pH, AM context. Best kept separate from PM strong-exfoliant actives; layering same-step with those can reduce efficacy or increase irritation.

explicit_pairs.note: Use vitamin C in the AM and retinol at night rather than layering together.
